# RAR extraction fixtures

Test corpus for the `.rar` extraction path (`crates/libscoop/src/internal/archive.rs`,
`extract_rar`). Everything here is either generated by us or produced by WinRAR
from content we generate, so no archive carries an unclear redistribution
licence. See **Provenance** below.

`expected-trees.txt` is the **baseline**: for each archive, the relative path
set, which entries are directories, and the SHA-256 of every extracted file. It
encodes the behaviour of the C++ decoder the extraction path used before the
`rars` swap, so it is the contract the current path has to keep.
`rar_extraction_matches_the_golden_baseline` compares against it.

**Baseline tool history.** The trees were originally produced by the `unrar` 0.5
crate (a UnRAR 6.x generation). That crate is no longer a dependency of this
workspace — not even a dev one — so the baseline is now regenerated with
**WinRAR 7.23's `Rar.exe`** instead. Regenerating with it reproduced the
committed trees **byte for byte**, so the two decoder generations agree on this
corpus. See **Regenerating** below.

## Provenance

### Produced by WinRAR 7.23

Toolchain: **RAR 7.23 x64** (WinRAR 7.23, Trial),
`D:\App\Scoop\apps\winrar\current\Rar.exe`. Regenerate with
`crates/libscoop/tests/fixtures/rar/gen-fixtures.ps1`.

Content is generated deterministically by that script (fixed text plus a
32-bit LCG), so no checked-in input blobs are needed. Exact invocations, run
from inside the generated content directory:

| Archive | Invocation |
|---|---|
| `rar5-normal.rar` | `Rar.exe a -ma5 -m3 -ep1 -r -mt1 <out> *` |
| `rar5-solid.rar` | `Rar.exe a -ma5 -m5 -s -ep1 -r -mt1 <out> *` |
| `rar5-store.rar` | `Rar.exe a -ma5 -m0 -ep1 -r -mt1 <out> *` |
| `rar5-x86filter.rar` | `Rar.exe a -ma5 -m5 -mcx+ -qo- -ep1 -r -mt1 <out> *` |
| `rar5-encrypted.rar` | `Rar.exe a -ma5 -m3 -pSECRET -ep1 -r -mt1 <out> *` |
| `rar5-vol.rar` → `.part1/.part2/.part3` | `Rar.exe a -ma5 -m0 -v16k -ep1 -r -mt1 <out> *` |
| `rar5-truncated.rar` | first 2722 bytes of `rar5-normal.rar` |
| `traversal-rar5.rar` | see "Traversal fixture" below |

`rar5-x86filter.rar` carries a genuinely x86-filtered stream: its payload is
`hok-shim.exe` (this repository's own build artifact, 11 776 bytes), and the
generator **fails** unless `-mcx+` really produces a smaller archive than
`-mcx-` for that payload (measured 5337 < 5376). A hand-built synthetic PE does
*not* qualify — for that payload `-mcx+` and `-mcx-` both give 253 bytes, i.e.
no filter ran — which is why a real executable is used.

### Produced by the `rars` writer

RAR 7.23 **cannot create RAR4**: `Rar.exe a -ma4` fails with
`ERROR: Unknown option: ma4`, exit code 7. The RAR 1.5-4.x fixtures are
therefore written by `rars` 0.9.4 from content generated in
`crates/libscoop/examples/gen_rar_fixtures.rs` (same LCG as the PowerShell
script, using `Math.imul` there so both produce byte-identical payloads).
Regenerate with `cargo run -p libscoop --example gen_rar_fixtures`.

| Archive | Shape |
|---|---|
| `rar4-normal.rar` | stored/compressed mix, nested directories |
| `rar4-solid.rar` | `-s` solid |
| `rar4-store.rar` | all stored |
| `rar4-largepayloads.rar` | 16 KiB x86-shaped and delta-shaped payloads |
| `rar4-vol.rar` → `.r00/.r01` | split, old-style volume naming |

RAR4 volume sets must use the old naming (`x.rar`, `x.r00`, `x.r01`); WinRAR
7.23 refuses a `.partN.rar`-named RAR4 set outright.

### Traversal fixture

`traversal-rar5.rar` holds one stored member named `..\evil.txt`. No encoder
emits such a name — `rars`' own `Builder` refuses it via `validate_entry_name` —
so `make-traversal-fixture.cjs` derives it from a WinRAR archive whose member is
an 11-byte placeholder. Placeholder and traversal name are the same length, so
every size field stays valid; only the name bytes and the covering header CRC-32
change. Verified: `rar t` reports `All OK` and 7-Zip lists the member as
`..\evil.txt`.

Two format details were measured rather than assumed, because the obvious
reading is wrong:

* RAR5's header size field counts the header bytes **after** the size vint, not
  including it. The alternative reading fails WinRAR's own stored CRC-32 on
  every block.
* A quick-open record stores a verbatim second copy of the headers, and a reader
  may extract from that copy instead — so the source archive is built with
  `-qo-` and the edit would otherwise measure nothing.

## Coverage

| Fixture | Covers |
|---|---|
| `rar5-normal.rar` | RAR5 v6, mixed store/compress, nested dirs, non-ASCII names, empty file |
| `rar5-solid.rar` | RAR5 solid stream, table reuse across members |
| `rar5-store.rar` | RAR5 stored members |
| `rar5-x86filter.rar` | RAR5 **x86 filter** (engagement proven, above) |
| `rar5-encrypted.rar` | archive-level encryption (`-p`); no password ⇒ must be an `Err` |
| `rar5-vol.part*.rar` | RAR5 multivolume, new-style `.partN.rar` naming, member split across volumes |
| `rar5-truncated.rar` | corrupt/truncated input ⇒ must be an `Err`, never a panic |
| `traversal-rar5.rar` | member name escaping the destination |
| `rar4-normal.rar` | RAR4 container, Unpack29 compression, nested dirs |
| `rar4-solid.rar` | RAR4 solid |
| `rar4-store.rar` | RAR4 stored |
| `rar4-largepayloads.rar` | RAR4 compressed path over 16 KiB x86-shaped and delta-shaped payloads |
| `rar4-vol.rar/.r00/.r01` | RAR4 multivolume, old-style naming |

### Not covered (stated, not implied)

* **No committed delta/ARM/RARVM-filter fixture.** The only sources found for
  those were `rars`'/RARLAB test corpora whose redistribution terms are unclear,
  and neither WinRAR 7.23 nor the `rars` writer exposes a switch that reliably
  forces a delta or ARM filter. What a filtered stream does to the decoder is
  therefore covered only by the x86 case above. Out-of-band evidence for the
  other filters is recorded in the delivery report, not in this corpus.
* **No committed RAR 1.3/1.4 fixture**, for the same licensing reason.
* `rar4-largepayloads.rar` uses x86- and delta-shaped payloads, but whether the
  `rars` writer recorded a VM filter for them is **not** asserted — only its
  decoded bytes are.
* Non-ASCII member names are covered for **RAR5 only**. RAR 1.5-4.x has no
  reliable way to mark a name as UTF-8: measured, the two decoders disagree on
  such a name (the `unrar` backend decodes the stored UTF-8 bytes against the OEM
  code page and yields bytes that are not a legal Windows filename), so a
  non-ASCII RAR4 member cannot serve as a parity baseline.

### How the former backend differed on traversal

The C++ backend this path used to have sanitised `..` to `_` inside `unrar`, so
`extract_rar`'s own `ParentDir` guard never fired for it and `..\evil.txt` landed
*inside* the destination as `.._evil.txt`. The current backend does not sanitise,
so it reaches the guard for real. Both satisfy the invariant that nothing is
written outside the destination, which is what
`rar_traversal_never_writes_outside_the_destination` pins; the old behaviour is
recorded here because it is easy to mistake that guard for one that worked.

## Regenerating

```powershell
# 1. RAR5 archives + truncated derivative (needs WinRAR 7.23)
pwsh crates/libscoop/tests/fixtures/rar/gen-fixtures.ps1

# 2. traversal-rar5.rar
$rar = 'D:\App\Scoop\apps\winrar\current\Rar.exe'
$tmp = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'trav-src'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $tmp | Out-Null
Set-Content "$tmp\abcdefghijk" 'traversal probe payload' -NoNewline
Push-Location $tmp; & $rar a -ma5 -m0 -qo- -ep1 "$tmp\src.rar" abcdefghijk; Pop-Location
node crates/libscoop/tests/fixtures/rar/make-traversal-fixture.cjs `
  "$tmp\src.rar" crates/libscoop/tests/fixtures/rar/traversal-rar5.rar

# 3. RAR4 archives (needs no WinRAR)
cargo run -p libscoop --example gen_rar_fixtures

# 4. baseline trees, extracted with WinRAR's Rar.exe
#    HOK_RAR_EXE overrides the extractor path; the default is
#    D:\App\Scoop\apps\winrar\current\Rar.exe
$env:HOK_RAR_EXE = 'D:\App\Scoop\apps\winrar\current\Rar.exe'
cargo test -p libscoop --lib rar_regenerate_golden_baseline -- --ignored
```

Step 4 is `#[ignore]`d, so neither CI nor a plain `cargo test` needs WinRAR. It
prints the path it wrote. If the extractor is missing it fails loudly with the
path it looked for and a pointer to where to get WinRAR — it never skips
silently, because a skipped regeneration would look like a pass.

After running it, **diff the result**: `expected-trees.txt` is the contract the
extraction path is held to, so any changed line needs reading before it is
accepted. A regeneration that changes nothing but the header comment is the
expected outcome for a tool-only change.

## Why the baseline is a file

The decoder that produced it — the `unrar` crate — was not safe to call
repeatedly in one process. Measured on this suite, driving it over all ten
parity fixtures aborted inside a core unsafe-precondition check
(`ptr::copy_nonoverlapping requires that both pointer arguments are aligned and
non-null`) or with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` in roughly 1 run in 20; any single
fixture survived 40 consecutive extractions, and serialising the tests did not
remove it. It is a process-level memory-safety abort, so it cannot be caught or
retried.

Freezing the reference output into a committed golden file therefore serves
three purposes: the always-run suite never drives a foreign decoder at all, the
baseline it compares against is reviewable in the diff, and — now that
regeneration goes through `Rar.exe` — **no C++ toolchain and no third-party Rust
RAR crate is needed to build or test this workspace**.

`expected-trees.txt` contains extracted file contents only as SHA-256 digests.
No third-party archive, executable or document is redistributed here other than
`hok-shim.exe`'s bytes embedded inside `rar5-x86filter.rar`, which is this
repository's own build output.
